# PRD: Data Storage, Sync & Offline

**Status:** Live
**Last updated:** 2026-05-06 (**Freeze + RLS integration:** frozen tables now enable RLS and get four policies generated by `regenerate_frozen_model_artifacts` — `frozen_view` / `frozen_insert` / `frozen_update` / `frozen_delete` — that mirror the records-table policies. Two new helper functions `wassell_can_view_jsonb` and `wassell_can_edit_jsonb` build a synthetic `records` row from the frozen-table columns and delegate to the existing `wassell_record_passes_scope` evaluator, so per-profile view_scope and edit_scope rules referencing scalar fields keep working after a model is frozen. Multi-value fields are intentionally omitted from the policy's `jsonb_build_object(...)` for performance — scope conditions on multiselect/lookup/table fail closed on frozen tables in v1 (documented limitation). The Phase 1 `created_by_user_id` column flows through too: `record_save(model_id, id, data, created_by)` gained a fourth parameter (DEFAULT NULL — backward-compatible), `freeze_apply_row` accepts it and COALESCE-preserves on update, `freeze_copy_records` carries the value when migrating records to the frozen table, and the `<name>_v` views + `unified_records` UNION surface it as a top-level column. Junction tables enforce parent-row reachability via an `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM <parent> WHERE id = record_id)` policy.) | 2026-05-05 (**Freeze (model promotion to dedicated table) — new:** every model can be promoted from a JSONB row in the unified `records` table to its own physical Postgres table with proper typed columns + junction tables for multi-value fields + subtables for `table` fields. One-way per model — once frozen, the Builder UI is read-only and future schema edits go through a migration written by Claude. Custom-UI models (`chats`, `ai_chats`) are excluded. Implementation is in `supabase/schema.sql` ("FREEZE INFRASTRUCTURE" section): the `freeze_model(model_id)` RPC validates the model, runs `freeze_check_coercion` (which surfaces any rows that can't be coerced — abort + report rather than silently NULL'ing), generates the parent table + junctions/subtables, copies records via `freeze_copy_records` + `freeze_apply_row`, drops the legacy `v_<name>` view, mints a JSONB-shape view `<name>_v` via `regenerate_frozen_model_artifacts`, marks the model `is_hardcoded=true` + `table_name=<name>`, deletes the original rows from `records`, and rebuilds the `unified_records` UNION view via `rebuild_unified_records`. Reads are unified through that view (UNION ALL of `records` + each frozen `<name>_v`); writes go through the `record_save(model_id, id, data)` / `record_delete(model_id, id)` SQL RPCs that dispatch on `is_hardcoded`. A `records_block_frozen_writes` trigger guards the original table — direct `.from('records').upsert()` for a frozen model raises a loud error pointing at the dispatcher RPC. Auto-IDs (`auto_id` field type) on frozen tables move from the JSONB-counter to a Postgres sequence per (model, field), eliminating the read-modify-write race. Multi-value fields (`multiselect`, multi-`lookup`, `table`) live in junction/subtables joined back into JSONB by the `<name>_v` view so the app's mental model stays "records as JSONB". The store branches `saveRecord` / `deleteRecord` through the dispatcher RPCs for frozen models and reads from `unified_records` in `initialize()`. The Builder's ModelEditor shows a "Freeze" button (with a coercion-preview modal) for unfrozen freezable models, and a "Frozen" pill + read-only banner once frozen — the SectionManager / CardBuilder / MapsBuilder / CustomButtonsTab tabs all accept a `readOnly` prop that blocks pointer events when set. The Builder Agent's schema-mutating tools (add/update/delete section + field, delete model) refuse to act on frozen models and direct the user to ask Claude (in a regular Claude Code chat) to write a migration.) | 2026-04-18 (storage shape for multi-select lookup + mirrored sections; migration v7; system models no longer overwritten on reload — Builder edits are authoritative; `section_mirror` field type storage)

## What it is (in plain English)
All of the app's data — models, records, workflows, dashboards, users, settings — is stored in a Supabase PostgreSQL database, with the flexible parts (schemas, record data, widget configs) held as JSONB. Every save is **mirrored to the browser's localStorage first** so the user sees an instant response, and then synced to Supabase in the background. If Supabase isn't configured at all, the app works fully offline against localStorage alone.

## Why it exists
Real-estate offices in Saudi Arabia sometimes have spotty connectivity. We don't want a hang during save. The localStorage-first approach gives instant feedback, and the JSONB-in-Postgres approach lets us ship schema changes (new field types, new workflow actions) without a DB migration.

## Key behaviors
- **6 Supabase tables:** `models`, `model_groups`, `records`, `workflows`, `dashboards`, `model_views`.
- **JSONB columns** hold the variable parts:
  - `models.schema` — the full sections/fields/options tree. `ModelField.is_multi` (optional bool) toggles a `lookup` field into multi-select mode. `ModelSection.is_mirrored` + `mirror_via_lookup_field_id` + `mirror_source_section_id` mark a section as mirrored from another model (local `fields` stays empty).
  - `models.card_config` — card view layout
  - `records.data` — field-slug → value map. Single-select lookup stores a `string` (record id); multi-select lookup (`is_multi: true`) stores a `string[]`. Mirror fields and mirrored sections store **nothing** — values are derived at render time by `mirrorResolver` / `sectionMirrorResolver`. `section_mirror` fields store a `Record<childSlug, value>` of **local overrides** only — any child value whose sync-back is on bypasses this map and flows into the linked record via the standard mirrored-section fan-out on save.
  - `workflows.definition` — trigger + conditions + actions
  - `dashboards.widgets` — widget configs + layout
  - `model_views.field_ids` / `model_views.conditions` — per-user saved table view (columns + filters)
- **Save path:**
  1. Update Zustand store in memory (UI re-renders).
  2. Write to localStorage synchronously (instant persistence).
  3. Fire-and-forget sync to Supabase (`.upsert()`); errors are toasted but don't block the UI.
- **Mirrored-section write-back:** when saving a record that contains mirrored sections, `RecordFormPage` first calls `saveRecord` on each linked target record (merging pending mirror edits into its `data`) **before** saving the current record. This fans one user action out to multiple records — always in the same Save click, never piecemeal.
- **Load path:**
  1. Try Supabase first on `initialize()`.
  2. If Supabase is not configured OR the fetch fails, fall back to localStorage.
  3. If neither has data, seed from `src/data/seedModels.ts` and `src/data/seedUsers.ts`.
  4. Run pending schema migrations (`src/lib/schemaMigrations.ts`) to reshape stored data when the schema evolves.
  5. Run an idempotent heal pass that re-attaches orphaned project system models to the Projects group and re-seeds the group if it was deleted. This runs on every load (not gated by schema version), because a user can orphan models by deleting the Projects group in the Builder.
  6. **Run `refreshSystemModels` on every load.** Inserts any system model from `SEED_MODELS` that isn't already in the user's store (so new default models added in code reach existing installs). Does NOT overwrite system models that already exist — **Builder edits to system models are authoritative and persist across reloads and deploys**, exactly like custom models. To propagate a structural change to a system model that already exists in an install, add a versioned migration in `schemaMigrations.ts` (the `migration_N_to_M` pattern). Non-system models are untouched.
- **Stable group IDs for system groups:** the Projects group uses a hardcoded UUID (`PROJECTS_GROUP_ID` in `seedModels.ts`). Re-seeding the group always produces the same id, so stored models' `group_id` references survive a wipe-and-reseed.
- **Supabase configured via env:** `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` and `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. If missing, the client is a no-op shim.
- **All IDs** are UUIDs (via `uuid` package).
- **Dates** are stored as ISO strings.
- **Field slugs** (the `name` prop) are snake_case.
- **No server-side validation or RLS is assumed yet** — the client is the trust boundary. Worth hardening later.

### Frozen models (added 2026-05-05)
- **Two storage shapes** coexist in the database. Unfrozen models still live as JSONB rows in the unified `records` table. **Frozen models** live in their own physical table `<model.name>` with proper typed columns, plus per-multi-value-field junction or subtables `<model>__<field>`.
- The `models.is_hardcoded` boolean (default `false`) tells you which shape a given model uses; `models.table_name` holds the physical table name when frozen (equals `model.name` for everything frozen through the standard pipeline).
- **Reads always go through the `unified_records` view** — a `UNION ALL` of `records` (for unfrozen models) and each frozen model's `<name>_v` JSONB-shape view. Same row shape (`id, model_id, data, created_by_user_id, created_at, updated_at`), so consumers don't need to branch.
- **Writes go through SQL RPCs:** `record_save(model_id, id, data, created_by)` upserts; `record_delete(model_id, id)` deletes. Both dispatch internally on `is_hardcoded` — frozen models hit their dedicated table via `freeze_apply_row` (which splits the JSONB payload into parent UPDATE + junction/subtable replace), unfrozen models hit `records` directly. The frontend store wraps these in `supabaseRecordUpsert` / `supabaseRecordDelete` (replacing the old direct `supabaseUpsert('records', ...)` calls in `saveRecord` / `deleteRecord`). `p_created_by` is COALESCE-preserved on update — first save stamps, edits don't overwrite — same posture as the records-table flow.
- **RLS on frozen tables (added 2026-05-06):** frozen tables enable RLS and get four policies generated by `regenerate_frozen_model_artifacts`. They reuse the same `wassell_user_has_action` model-perm helper as the records-table policies, plus two new helpers `wassell_can_view_jsonb` / `wassell_can_edit_jsonb` that build a synthetic `records` row literal from the frozen-table columns and delegate to the existing `wassell_record_passes_scope` evaluator. Per-profile view_scope and edit_scope rules referencing scalar fields keep working after a model is frozen. Multi-value fields (multiselect, multi-lookup, table) are intentionally NOT included in the synthetic JSONB — junction joins inside an RLS expression evaluate per-row and would tank reads. Scope conditions on multi-value fields fail closed on frozen tables; this is a known v1 limitation. Junction tables get their own `frozen_junction_view` / `frozen_junction_write` policies that gate via `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM <parent> WHERE id = record_id)`, so reaching into a junction inherits the parent's RLS verdict.
- **Field-type → physical mapping** (used by both `freeze_model` for DDL and `freeze_apply_row` for writes):
  - `text` / `textarea` / `email` / `phone` / `url` / `dropdown` / `auto_id` / `lookup` (single) → `text` column
  - `number` / `currency` / `formula` → `numeric`
  - `date` / `datetime` → `timestamptz`
  - `checkbox` → `boolean`
  - `range` → expanded into `<name>_min`, `<name>_max` numeric columns
  - `notes` / `section_mirror` / `section_selector` / `assignee` → `jsonb` (kept structured)
  - `multiselect` → junction `<model>__<field>` with `(record_id uuid, value text, PK)`
  - `lookup is_multi=true` → junction `<model>__<field>` with `(record_id uuid, target_record_id uuid, PK)`
  - `table` → subtable `<model>__<field>` with `(id, record_id, row_index, ...row columns)`
  - `mirror` → SKIPPED (computed at runtime from sibling lookup; no physical column)
- **Coercion failures abort the freeze.** `freeze_check_coercion(model_id)` returns the rows that can't coerce (e.g. a "number" field with junk text); the freeze SQL function aborts with a descriptive error if any are present. The Builder modal previews these failures BEFORE the user confirms so they can clean up records first. We never silently NULL data on freeze.
- **Auto-IDs on frozen tables** switch from the JSONB `auto_id_counters` map (which had a documented race condition) to a Postgres `SEQUENCE` per (model, auto_id field), seeded at freeze time above the high-water mark of any existing IDs. Same display format (`CLT-001`); no more race.
- **Records-table guard.** A `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE` trigger on `records` raises a loud exception if anyone tries to write to it for a frozen model. The dispatcher RPCs route correctly; this is a safety net for forgotten direct `.from('records').upsert()` calls in legacy code paths so they fail loudly instead of silently writing to a table the app no longer reads.
- **Server-side reads** in `api/` and `supabase/functions/` use `unified_records`. Writes use the `record_save` RPC. Writes to `chats` records (always unfrozen — excluded from Freeze) keep using `.from('records')` directly since the trigger only fires for frozen models.
- **Builder UI for frozen models is read-only.** The "Freeze" button is replaced with a "Frozen · `<name>`" pill plus a banner explaining schema edits go through Claude. The Fields/Card/Maps/Buttons tabs all accept a `readOnly` prop that blocks pointer events. The Builder Agent's schema-mutating tools refuse on frozen models with a message pointing the user at a regular Claude Code chat for migrations.
- **Future schema edits** (adding/dropping a column, adding a new junction) happen via a migration written by Claude that does the DDL AND updates the model's JSONB schema in `models.schema`, then calls `regenerate_frozen_model_artifacts(model_id)` + `rebuild_unified_records()` to refresh the view + UNION.

## User flows
1. **First-run offline:** User opens app with no Supabase env → app seeds from `seedModels.ts` → all data lives in localStorage → fully functional.
2. **First-run online:** User opens app with Supabase configured → app queries tables → if empty, seeds → otherwise loads existing data.
3. **Normal save:** User clicks Save → UI updates instantly → Supabase upsert resolves seconds later in the background.
4. **Offline edit while online was expected:** User loses connection → saves still succeed locally → next successful Supabase call doesn't currently replay queued changes (see limitations).

## Data touched
- Tables: `models`, `model_groups`, `records`, `workflows`, `dashboards` (and if wired: `users`, `roles`, `profiles`, `translations`).
- `localStorage` keys: one per store slice.
- Supabase storage bucket for file-type field uploads.

## Key files
| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `src/lib/supabase.ts` | Client init (no-op if env missing) |
| `src/stores/appStore.ts` | All load/save logic, localStorage mirror, Supabase sync, heal on init |
| `src/lib/schemaMigrations.ts` | Versioned migrations + heal pass. Current `SCHEMA_VERSION = 7` (v7 wipes old follow-up records, refreshes Clients schema for multi-select lookups, and inserts Appointments + Units models for returning users) |
| `src/data/seedModels.ts` | Seed content for first-run (incl. stable `PROJECTS_GROUP_ID`; exports `appointmentsId` and `unitsId`) |
| `src/data/seedUsers.ts` | Demo users |
| `src/lib/mirrorResolver.ts` | Mirror-field resolution (single + multi-select sibling support) |
| `src/lib/sectionMirrorResolver.ts` | Mirrored-section resolution (sibling lookup → source section + target record) |
| `supabase/` | SQL schema (`schema.sql`) |
| `.env.example` | Documents required env vars |

## Open questions / known limitations
- **No offline queue replay:** edits made while offline are in localStorage but won't auto-push when connectivity returns — a full page refresh is needed to trigger a re-sync path.
- **No conflict resolution:** last write wins; two users editing the same record at once will silently overwrite each other.
- **No row-level security policies** configured in Supabase yet — any anon key holder has full table access.
- **No real-time subscriptions** — changes from other clients aren't pushed until the page reloads.
- **JSONB size** — very large models or records could exceed practical JSONB limits; no guardrails.
